title: Leetcode
body:
# LeetCode patterns Use this as a routing guide: identify the input shape and the operation the question is asking for, then open the matching pattern. Many problems fit more than one pattern, so follow the first clue that is central to the solution. ## Before choosing a pattern Turn the prompt into four concrete answers before writing code: 1. **What is the state?** An index, a pair of pointers, a window, a graph node, or a DP state. 2. **What makes a partial answer valid?** This is the loop invariant; preserve it after every iteration. 3. **What ends the search?** Reaching an index, emptying a queue, finding a target, or filling a DP table. 4. **What must be returned?** A value, a count, a boolean, a path, or all valid constructions. Then name the constraints. `n <= 20` often permits backtracking or a bitmask; `n ~= 10^5` usually needs O(n) or O(n log n). A static array permits prefix sums, while updates need a tree structure. Ask whether input may be reordered or mutated before sorting or marking cells in place. ## Start with the input ### Is it an [[Array]] or [[Strings|string]] problem? - Need many sums over fixed ranges? [[Prefix Sum|Use prefix sums]]. - Need a pair, a palindrome check, or values moving inward from two ends? [[Two Pointers|Use two pointers]]. - Need a best/valid contiguous subarray or substring? [[Sliding Window|Use a sliding window]]. - Need each value's next greater or smaller value? [[Monotonic Stack|Use a monotonic stack]]. - Need the largest, smallest, or most frequent `k` items? [[Top K Elements|Use a heap]]. - Is the data sorted, rotated-sorted, or asking for a boundary? [[Modified Binary Search|Use modified binary search]]. - Are the values time ranges or other start/end pairs? [[Overlapping Intervals|Use interval processing]]. - Need a complement, duplicate, running count, grouping, or fast lookup? [[Hash Map Pattern|Use a hash map or set]]. - Is a locally best choice provably safe after sorting? [[Greedy|Try a greedy scan]]. - Are you matching nested delimiters or undoing the most recent unfinished work? [[Stack and Queue|Use a stack or queue]]. ### Is it a [[Linked List]] problem? - Need the middle node, cycle detection, or the kth node from the end? [[Fast and Slow Pointers|Use fast and slow pointers]]. - Need to reverse, rotate, or reorder links with O(1) extra space? [[Linked List In-place Reversal|Reverse in place]]. ### Is it a [[Tree]] or [[Graph]] problem? - Need to visit every node in a particular tree order? [[Binary Tree Traversal|Choose a tree traversal]]. - Need to explore a path, detect a cycle, or count connected components? [[Depth First Search|Use DFS]]. - Need the fewest edges in an unweighted graph, or process one level at a time? [[Breadth First Search|Use BFS]]. - Is the graph represented as a grid or [[Matrix]]? [[Matrix Traversal|Traverse the matrix]]. - Need the shortest *weighted* path? [[Dijkstra's Algorithm|Use Dijkstra's algorithm]]. - Need to merge groups, test undirected connectivity, or detect a redundant edge? [[Union Find|Use union-find]]. - Need an ordering with prerequisites? [[Topological Sort|Use topological sort]]. ### Are you choosing among possibilities or reusing subproblems? - Need all permutations, combinations, placements, or puzzle states? [[Backtracking|Use backtracking]]. - Need an optimal value or count with repeated subproblems? [[Dynamic Programming|Use dynamic programming]]. - Need prefix/word lookup or character-by-character dictionary matching? [[Trie|Use a trie]]. - Is the input a small integer set, XOR/parity task, or subset enumeration? [[Bit Manipulation|Use bit operations]]. ## Quick chooser | Problem clue | Pattern | | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | Repeated range totals | [[Prefix Sum]] | | Contiguous segment | [[Sliding Window]] | | Sorted values, pair, or boundary | [[Two Pointers]] or [[Modified Binary Search]] | | Next larger/smaller item | [[Monotonic Stack]] | | Top or frequent `k` values | [[Top K Elements]] | | Links, nodes, and O(1) space | [[Fast and Slow Pointers]] or [[Linked List In-place Reversal]] | | Levels or minimum unweighted distance | [[Breadth First Search]] | | Paths or components | [[Depth First Search]] | | Exhaust every valid choice | [[Backtracking]] | | Reuse overlapping answers | [[Dynamic Programming]] | | Complement, duplicate, or frequency | [[Hash Map Pattern]] | | Sorted choices that stay optimal | [[Greedy]] | | Connectivity while adding edges | [[Union Find]] | | Prerequisite order | [[Topological Sort]] | | Weighted shortest path | [[Dijkstra's Algorithm]] | | Prefix or dictionary words | [[Trie]] | | XOR, masks, or parity | [[Bit Manipulation]] | ## Visual decision tree This Mermaid version adapts the [AlgoMonster flowchart](https://algo.monster/flowchart?path=graph%3Ano%7Csorted-search%3Ano%7Ckth-smallest%3Ano%7Clinked-list%3Ano%7Chash-table%3Ano%7Cintervals%3Ano%7Cpartition-array%3Ano%7Cstring-segmentation%3Ayes%7Cstring-pattern%3Ayes) into the local notes. Follow the labelled arrows; the highlighted route is the path in that link. ```mermaid flowchart TD start([Read the prompt and constraints]) --> is_graph{Is it a graph
or grid traversal?} is_graph -- Yes --> graph_patterns[[BFS · DFS · Matrix Traversal
Dijkstra · Union-Find · Topological Sort]] is_graph -- No --> sorted{Is it sorted, rotated,
or a monotonic search?} sorted -- Yes --> sorted_patterns[[Modified Binary Search
Two Pointers]] sorted -- No --> kth{Need the kth / top
smallest or largest item?} kth -- Yes --> kth_patterns[[Top K Elements
Heap or quickselect]] kth -- No --> linked{Is it a linked-list
pointer problem?} linked -- Yes --> linked_patterns[[Fast & Slow Pointers
In-place Reversal]] linked -- No --> hash{Does lookup by value,
frequency, or complement solve it?} hash -- Yes --> hash_patterns[[Hash Map / Set
Prefix Sum + Map]] hash -- No --> intervals{Are there start/end ranges
or scheduling conflicts?} intervals -- Yes --> interval_patterns[[Overlapping Intervals
Heap + Greedy]] intervals -- No --> partition{Can an array be split into
valid parts or choices?} partition -- Yes --> partition_patterns[[Dynamic Programming
Backtracking / Greedy]] partition -- No --> segment{Does a string need to be
segmented into dictionary words?} segment -- Yes --> pattern{Does the segment decision
depend on a character pattern?} segment -- No --> contiguous{Is the answer a contiguous
subarray or substring?} pattern -- Yes --> string_patterns[[String matching:
Trie · DP · Backtracking]] pattern -- No --> word_break[[Word Break:
DP or Trie]] contiguous -- Yes --> window[[Sliding Window
or Prefix Sum + Hash Map]] contiguous -- No --> choices{Must you try all choices
or reuse subproblems?} choices -- All choices --> backtrack[[Backtracking]] choices -- Reuse states --> dp[[Dynamic Programming]] classDef selected fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,stroke-width:3px,color:#713f12; class is_graph,sorted,kth,linked,hash,intervals,partition,segment,pattern selected; ``` The `No` route through **graph → sorted search → kth → linked list → hash table → intervals → partition array → string segmentation**, then `Yes` to **string pattern**, leads to the highlighted string-matching family. Use [[Trie]] for prefix/dictionary traversal, [[Dynamic Programming]] for word-break-style reuse, and [[Backtracking]] when all valid segmentations are required. ## Pattern combinations The strongest clue chooses the outer algorithm; a second pattern often supplies a data structure. | If the prompt says… | Start with… | Often combine with… | | --- | --- | --- | | “longest/shortest **contiguous** segment” | [[Sliding Window]] | [[Hash Map Pattern]] / frequency array | | “number of subarrays with sum/property” | [[Prefix Sum]] | [[Hash Map Pattern]] | | “all paths/combinations” | [[Backtracking]] or [[Depth First Search]] | pruning / a `used` set | | “minimum steps” | [[Breadth First Search]] | multi-source queue or parent map | | “minimum cost” | [[Dynamic Programming]] or [[Dijkstra's Algorithm]] | a heap / memoization | | “schedule/rooms/overlap” | [[Overlapping Intervals]] | [[Top K Elements|heap]] / greedy | | “subsequence” | [[Dynamic Programming]] | binary search or two pointers | ## A reliable solving loop 1. Write the brute-force idea and its cost. 2. Identify the repeated work or monotonic fact that removes it. 3. State the invariant in a short comment beside the loop. 4. Test empty input, one item, duplicates, all-equal values, and the first/last boundary. 5. Confirm time and space complexity against the constraints. Each linked page gives a recognition rule, a default outline, the variants that change the outline, and the edge cases that most often cause wrong answers.
